channel.title: Blockheight
channel.description: Blockheight reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: How to Check a Bridge Transfer to Manta Pacific
item.description: Check a Manta Pacific bridge transfer by matching its source transaction, route and wallet address, then confirm the destination credit in History or the network explorer.

item.title: How to Read PooCoin Token Prices at the Right Precision
item.description: PooCoin prices can look like zero when small tokens are rounded; read the quote, trading pair and order size together before treating displayed decimals as value.

item.title: BSC swap costs: how slippage, fees and gas work
item.description: A BSC swap’s cost combines pool fees, price impact and BNB gas; slippage tolerance sets the worst fill you accept, not a fee charged by the network.

item.title: Polygon Bridge timing depends on transfer direction
item.description: Polygon PoS deposits from Ethereum usually take minutes, while withdrawals back to Ethereum can take hours as they wait for checkpoints and a final claim.

item.title: Verify a Bridged ERC-20 Deposit on Both Chains
item.description: A bridged ERC-20 deposit is confirmed by matching the source transaction, destination token contract, recipient and amount across both chains—not by a wallet notification.

item.title: Token Metadata Pending: What to Check and How to Fix It
item.description: A pending label usually signals missing display data, not a failed transfer; check the contract, metadata URI and indexer before trying a refresh or changing settings.

item.title: Keep Cross-Chain Receipts Lean When Leaving an Exchange
item.description: When moving assets from an exchange, keep transaction IDs and status checkpoints for cross-chain transfers, then retrieve full receipt data only when you need it.

item.title: Crypto deposit windows set the payment deadline, not the network clock
item.description: A deposit window sets how long a crypto payment request remains valid; network confirmations and platform crediting run on separate clocks, affecting when funds arrive.

item.title: Bridge maintenance windows pause new token transfers
item.description: A planned bridge window pauses new token transfers while operators update or verify cross-chain systems; check route status and pending messages before sending.

item.title: Four checks before moving a deprecated wrapped token
item.description: A deprecated wrapped token may keep trading after support ends; check its address, redemption route and deadline before moving funds or approving it.

item.title: Why DeFi Token Approvals Add a Transaction and Gas Fee
item.description: An ERC-20 approval is a separate contract call with its own gas fee; allowance size controls token access, while network demand sets the fee paid.

item.title: XMR-to-Sepolia transfers need at least 10 Monero confirmations
item.description: ZeroFi’s XMR-to-Sepolia route requires 10 Monero confirmations, so the chain alone can take about 20 minutes; bridge processing and Sepolia delivery add variable time.

item.title: Why TRON Swap Liquidity Providers Can Lose Value
item.description: TRON swap LPs can finish with less value than holders when token prices diverge; pool mechanics, fees and price ranges determine whether providing liquidity pays.

item.title: How to Compare TRON USDT Swap Routes
item.description: Compare TRON USDT routes by net output, pool depth, slippage and network resource cost; a better quote can still leave less after fees when you execute.

item.title: How an Account Abstraction Wallet Handles a Bridge Route
item.description: An account abstraction wallet can package approvals and bridge calls, but each route still depends on chain support, fees, liquidity and destination settlement.

item.title: Cross-chain batching cuts wallet steps, not chain settlement
item.description: Cross-chain batching groups wallet actions into fewer transactions, but each chain still settles separately and may require its own approval and fee.

item.title: How treasury teams reconcile Manta Bridge transfers
item.description: Treasury teams can reconcile Manta Bridge transfers by matching both chains’ records, treating pending withdrawals as in transit and separating network fees.

item.title: Set a token spend limit before swapping from your wallet
item.description: A token approval lets a swap contract spend tokens from your wallet. Set a cap for the trade, then review any allowance left behind after the swap.

item.title: How to limit price risk when bridging XMR
item.description: An XMR bridge can expose a transfer to price moves before the swap settles. Control that window with quote checks, smaller transfers or a temporary hedge.

item.title: TRON swap permissions: how to spot unusual requests
item.description: A TRON swap may request a token allowance or contract call. Check the spender, amount, network and method before signing, then review access you no longer need.
